item.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education
item.description: Reproducing and modifying a meter-scale humanoid remains challenging for research and teaching groups with limited fabrication resources and engineering support. This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support.

item.title: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors
item.description: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control.

item.title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
item.description: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object.

item.title: Into My Arms: Structured reinforcement learning for autonomous transport of objects and humans
item.description: Whole-body humanoid manipulation remains bottlenecked by high-dimensional state-action spaces, contact-rich environments, and long task horizons. This trilemma is a challenge that state-of-the-art reinforcement learning (RL) methods are yet to resolve reliably.

item.title: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts
item.description: General-purpose manipulation robots must acquire new skills over time without forgetting prior ones or retraining from scratch. We present a continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network (PNN).

item.title: Optimizing Locally Equivalent Graph States in Quantum Computing Using Greedy Best-First Search
item.description: In measurement-based quantum computation and quantum repeater networks, graph-structured quantum states called graph states play a central role as an essential resource. In a graph state, each vertex corresponds to a qubit, and each edge is prepared by applying one controlled-Z (CZ) gate.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
item.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved substantial progress across many domains, but training an agent \textit{tabula rasa} remains highly sample-inefficient. A common remedy is to initialize the agent using a neural network pretrained on demonstrations.
